A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UPO research, with matching authors, architecture, principal experiments and theoretical framework. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results on Sudoku, Zebra, GSM8K and MATH500, plus training-dynamics and regularization experiments in Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds reward ablations, Natural Questions experiments, learned-policy Pass@N results and Sudoku case studies.

M1.justification: The frozen-MDM architecture, UPO loss and reference-policy realizations remain intact. Appendices D.2–D.3 introduce limited adaptations: training with Qwen-3 32B log-likelihood rewards and noise-perturbed position selection for multi-shot generation. Newly disclosed details of the retained experiments do not establish that their underlying implementation changed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates logic puzzles and mathematical reasoning on four benchmarks. v2 retains these and adds Natural Questions in Appendix D.2, substantially extending the represented domain to open-domain question answering and unconstrained natural-language answers.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain random, margin, entropy and confidence sampling, and Figure 3 retains the unregularized, randomly initialized policy comparison. New analyses reuse existing heuristics. Qwen-3 32B supplies rewards rather than serving as an evaluated competing generation method.

E3.justification: v2 adds binary-versus-dense reward controls, an ARM-likelihood reward and measurement protocol, and learned-policy Pass@N evaluation with controlled sampling noise. Section 4.1 also revises the stated mathematical-reasoning reward from binary correctness alone to correctness plus likelihood shaping. This changes the reported setting without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's reference-policy, regularization and diffu-GRPO analyses, v2 tests binary versus dense rewards, learning without correctness rewards, and the learned policy's multi-shot behavior in Appendix D. Appendix F adds two stepwise Sudoku case studies examining error propagation and premature position selection.

E5.justification: Neither version reports replication seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 4's within-group reward mean and standard deviation are retained. The newly specified GRPO group size of six is a training setting, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their numerical results. New Table 4 reports binary-reward accuracies of 80.1% on Sudoku and 70.1% on GSM8K, alongside the retained dense-reward scores of 81.7% and 70.3%. Appendix D.2 reports 70.5% GSM8K accuracy against its stated 68.2% confidence baseline, and new figures report likelihood trends, Pass@N behavior and qualitative trajectories. These are additional results, not demonstrated same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The existing theoretical framework receives targeted refinements. Theorem 2 changes non-strict KL tightening to strict tightening with explicit binary-reward and nondegeneracy conditions. Appendix C adds terminal-support and trajectory absolute-continuity arguments, corrects Proposition 2's strict inequality to a non-strict bound, and repairs local algebra and indexing.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding contribution statement retain the central claims: learn unmasking policies for frozen MDMs through a regularized MDP, provide convergence and KL-tightening guarantees, and outperform strong heuristics across the four principal benchmarks. The additional studies support and qualify this contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion. It explains smaller mathematical-reasoning gains through weaker ordering regularity, vocabulary size and training-data limitations; interprets the theorem's reward conditions; and frames general-purpose policy learning as preliminary. Appendix F adds distinct explanations of confidence-sampling failures, while Appendix D discusses reward-density and exploration tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a stated code-access link and Appendix E with optimizer settings, group size, learning-rate schedules, regularization coefficients, GPU allocations, quantization, checkpoint selection and prompt templates. It also documents likelihood-reward ranking, Zebra supervised fine-tuning and argmax token selection. These fill substantial omissions in v1's reproducibility information without proving those settings were newly adopted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Qwen3, Natural Questions, Gumbel-Softmax, planted constraint-satisfaction hardness and Seed Diffusion, with localized discussion connecting them to the additions. Its principal positioning relative to MDM post-training and DCOLT remains unchanged. Publication and bibliographic updates otherwise concern the same cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. v2 adds localized explanations, an expanded conclusion discussion, a contents page, conference statements and new appendix sections, while polishing cross-references and proof exposition. The header changes from preprint to ICLR 2026 publication status.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 and Figures 6–10, introducing reward-comparison plots, likelihood curves, learned-policy Pass@N visualization and detailed Sudoku trajectories. It also adds boxed prompt templates and colored proof parentheses, and relocates existing displays. The original figures and tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility and validation: Appendix E supplies previously missing reward construction, training settings and prompts, while Table 4 tests the binary-reward regime assumed by the theory. Appendix C corrects and strengthens mathematical justification, and the trajectory analyses explain concrete failures. The Natural Questions evidence remains preliminary, and Appendix D.3's Gaussian-noise formula conflicts with its Gumbel-Softmax label, but these localized weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial documentation and validation gains.
